# DeepSeek Harness Remote Control (DSH RC)

**Remote access to your DeepSeek Harness desktop, through one TLS WebSocket and
the browser you alre

cess to your DeepSeek Harness desktop, through one TLS WebSocket and
the browser you already have.**
**A project by Ts. Dr. Leong Yee Rock · VYROX International Sdn Bhd · VYROX AI**

DSH RC serves the *unmodified* Harness web UI over a single outbound
connection. The desktop agent d

ials the edge; the edge proxies HTTP and
WebSocket streams to it; your browser opens the real DSH in

terface. No WebRTC,
no UDP, no inbound port, no port forwarding, and no second client to install on
the machine in front of you.

Works on **macOS, Windows and Linux**, for both steps. Install DeepSeek Harness
and open it once on

each computer. Then paste one prompt into DeepSeek Harness
and its agent does everything else: downl

oad, install, set up, connect and
restart. Or run the one command for your system yourself.

## Architecture
[代码示例省略，未执行]

- **Browser → edge:** ordinary HTTPS/WSS on 443. Sub-path mount
`/d/<deviceId>/`; the app's own rela

tive URLs and `<base href="./">` do the
rest.
- **Edge → agent:** one WebSocket per device, multiple

xed into independent HTTP
and WebSocket streams, with per-stream flow control and a weighted schedul

er
(high/normal/low) so bulk traffic cannot starve the UI.
- **Agent → DSH:** `127.0.0.1:<port>` onl

y, with a cookie obtained from the DSH
launch token. The token and cookie never leave the desktop.

Details: ARCHITECTURE.md ·
PROTOCOL.md ·
ADR-0001: no WebRTC ·
ADR-0002: native remote sessions.
## Requirements
| Component | Requirement |

| Desktop | DeepSeek Harness **0.2.1-rc.3** (plugin declares `>=0.2.1-rc.3 <0.3.1`) |
| Edge | Node.
js ≥ 24.0 (tested with **24.22.1**; or the Docker image), a domain for TLS in production. `install.s

h host` / `install.ps1` set up a macOS, Windows or Linux host as a background service |
| Browser |

Any current Chromium, Firefox or Safari |
| Network | Outbound 443 from the desktop; no inbound port

Chromium, Firefox or Safari |
| Network | Outbound 443 from the desktop; no inbound ports, no UDP |
## Security in one paragraph

TLS to the edge; **device secrets are 32 random bytes stored only as SHA-256**;
the embed ticket use

d by the native remote window is one-time, device-targeted
and expires in 60 seconds; the resulting

edge session is short-lived. The **DSH launch token
never leaves the desktop**: the agent exchanges

it once for a loopback-bound
cookie held in memory. The browser never receives a Harness credential,

and the
agent refuses non-loopback upstreams, absolute URLs, `..` segments and encoded
traversal ev

en if the edge is compromised. The edge sees proxied plaintext;
self-host it if that matters. Residu

al risk and the full STRIDE pass:
THREAT-MODEL.md. Report issues per
SECURITY.md.
## What it deliberately does not do

- **No mobile apps.** The browser is the client.
- **No WebRTC data path in v1.** See ADR-0001 for
t

he trade-off and the conditions under which that changes.
- **No replay of Harness mutations** after

an unknown outcome.
- **No second chat/files/terminal UI.** That is the point.
- **No multi-tenant

SaaS.** Self-host first; hosted accounts and OAuth are
roadmap, not v1.
